purposes.statement: Help an individual keep in touch with selected people at a personally meaningful frequency and depth, while respecting both people's autonomy.
purposes.intendedChange: More wanted contact and less effort remembering or initiating it.
successCriteria: More wanted contact happens with the people the owner chose to keep in touch with.
Less effort is needed to remember or initiate contact.
Both people's autonomy is respected; unwanted pressure does not rise.
nonGoals: Time spent in the app (diagnostic measure only)
Streak penalties, public relationship scores and group discussion (spec §3)
constraints: Private contacts, goals and notes stay owner-only; connecting accounts adds consensual sharing capabilities and does not turn private notes or goals into shared data.
The app can help before any friend installs it.

externals.external: The events themselves and the owner's private calendars

claims.name: Remembering
claims.mechanism: Private context and a chosen cadence reduce forgetting
claims.indicator: Weekly proportion of active goals satisfied by qualifying contact; denominator excludes paused goals
claims.evaluationMethod: Two-week personal baseline where the user chooses, then a four-week pilot; compare descriptive trends and interview participants. A later randomized or staggered comparison with consent and a defined outcome protocol can test T1-T3.
claims.limitation: Missing baseline remains unknown; a before-and-after improvement cannot establish causality; no numerical effect target is set. Does not assume more frequent contact always improves a relationship.

claims.name: Initiating
claims.mechanism: One concrete next action lowers initiation effort
claims.indicator: User-rated effort before and after use
claims.evaluationMethod: Two-week personal baseline, then a four-week pilot; compare descriptive trends and interview participants.
claims.limitation: A channel opened is not proof that contact occurred; before-and-after change cannot establish causality.

claims.name: Meaning
claims.mechanism: User-defined depth prompts help contact feel worthwhile
claims.evaluationMethod: Optional reflection collected during the four-week pilot against the two-week baseline; later randomized or staggered comparison with consent.
claims.limitation: Avoid treating a model's rating as relationship truth; missing baseline remains unknown.

claims.name: Autonomy
claims.mechanism: Adjustable cadence, pauses and recipient consent reduce unwanted pressure
claims.indicator: Notification burden, snoozes, opt-outs and private burden reports
claims.evaluationMethod: Four-week pilot with private burden reports against the two-week baseline; interview participants.
claims.limitation: Blocking is not a product failure; before-and-after change cannot establish causality.

claims.name: Updates later
claims.mechanism: Consented digest reading provides context for a personal follow-up
claims.outcome: Readers have context that supports a personal follow-up
claims.indicator: Reader usefulness and subsequent voluntary contact
claims.evaluationMethod: Deferred until the digest interpretation is accepted and the module is enabled.
claims.limitation: Passive reading never counts as personal contact by default.

description.narrative: The main experience is a purposeful contacts app. People are the organizing unit. Each relationship has an owner-only intention such as “check in every two weeks” or “make room for a proper conversation monthly.” A calm Today view suggests a finite set of next actions. A user can act, log contact, snooze, pause or revise the goal. There are no streak penalties or public relationship scores.

features.name: Consented pair connections
features.summary: Invitation-based pairs formed by two explicit consents; either party can disconnect or block.

features.name: Private contacts
features.summary: Keep a private contact record before any friend installs the app; optional channel and context.

features.name: Cadence and depth
features.summary: An owner-only goal with an interval and a desired depth

features.name: Suggested next actions
features.summary: A finite Today view of at most five due suggestions; opening a channel never completes a goal.

features.name: Digests and photo suggestions (later)
features.summary: Later digests and photo suggestions; realization deferred while the digest interpretation is unresolved.

commitments.statement: A finite incoming view - Today returns at most five suggestions; many independent senders appear in one owner's finite inbox.
No streak penalties, public relationship scores or group discussion belong in the core contract.
One-to-one actions - exactly one recipient per draft, send request or private reply; no recipient list, bulk send or group thread.
Owner-defined cadence and depth - goals are owner-only; depth labels are the owner's, not a global quality ranking.
Personal control over initiating contact - opening a channel needs a user gesture and never completes a goal; no autonomous send.

alternatives: Reader-driven digest publication (proposed interpretation): an author publishes an owned edition and approved subscribers independently read it; replies remain one-to-one and readers cannot see or address one another.
Retain only individually addressed updates, if “no one-to-many outgoing” prohibits all shared digest visibility.
Shared intentions - two people agree on a joint contact rhythm as a new consented object that never exposes either private goal.
openQuestions: Digest interpretation: this still distributes one author's information to many people. If “no one-to-many outgoing” prohibits all such visibility, shared digests conflict with it. Digest realization stays blocked until that interpretation is accepted.
Photo suggestions need a device capability adapter, local or provider processing and an approval contract before any upload or send.
Groups need their own Purpose, membership and topology contract and an accepted Evolution; disabled in this System.
Live messaging may need Durable Objects only if a later messaging Evolution requires coordinated live state.

requirements.title: Core scope
requirements.text: the app must provide private contacts, goals, contact logging, invitation-based pair connections, in-app due prompts and settings. Direct in-app messaging, subscriptions, digests, media automation and groups must remain disabled in the core scope. Opening an external channel must require a user gesture; unsupported channels must offer copyable contact details.

requirements.title: Due dates
requirements.text: the app must use local calendar dates in the owner's IANA time zone. The anchor must be the latest qualifying event date, or the goal creation date when none exists. dueDate must equal anchor plus intervalDays. A goal must become due when today's date reaches dueDate, unless paused or snoozed until a later date. Revising a goal must not create a ContactEvent. Date and time-zone fixtures must cover daylight-saving changes.

requirements.title: Goal qualification
requirements.text: an enabled goal must have intervalDays from 1 through 3650 and desiredDepth in light, meaningful or shared-time. These are the owner's labels, not a global quality ranking. A ContactEvent must qualify only when the owner explicitly marks that it met this goal. The app must record the goal ID and desiredDepth at confirmation and count only qualifications matching the current desiredDepth. Changing depth may change which historical events qualify; SchedulePreview must show that effect before saving. Editing or deleting an event must recompute the schedule.

requirements.title: Operations
requirements.text: all mutations must authorize the authenticated owner or explicit connected capability at the server, validate inputs and support an idempotency key. Creation must return an immutable ID and version. Reads and writes to another owner's private records must return a non-revealing denial. Concurrent stale-version edits must return conflict without overwriting current data. Each operation row below defines required preconditions and effects.

requirements.title: Concurrency and revocation
requirements.text: invite redemption must survive two concurrent accept requests without two pairs or two redemptions. Read and send authorization must check revocation against current authoritative state. Already delivered external messages or copied data remain outside our ability to retract.

requirements.title: Authentication
requirements.text: sensitive token routes must not leak tokens through analytics or referrers. Login continuation must preserve a validated invitation without consuming it. A pinned authentication Kit must specify the identity provider and its callback routes before realization.

requirements.title: Screens
requirements.text: authenticated screens must share one AppShell containing exactly TopBar, PrimaryNav and RouteOutlet. PrimaryNav must contain Today, People and Settings. Counts below specify required RouteOutlet composition, excluding the shell. All private screens must show one StatePanel for loading or fatal error in place of loaded content. Forms must keep entered values after recoverable validation or network errors and render one ErrorSummary when needed.

requirements.title: Today prompts
requirements.text: Today must return at most five suggestions, ordered by effective due date then stable goal ID. There must be at most one open suggestion per goal version and due cycle. Logging qualifying contact must resolve its suggestion. Snoozing must update its effective due date; pausing must suppress prompts. Blocking a linked counterpart must pause the blocker's corresponding goal and suppress its suggestions. In-app reminders are required. Optional external reminders, when enabled, must be limited to one owner notification per local day containing a link without contact details. Reminder delivery must recheck preferences and cancellations.

criteria.title: System structure is complete
criteria.claim: Require exactly one app Thing, thing.webapp, with a specification and artifact.webapp binding; require Purpose, Externals, Theory and ontology references. Reject dangling references or domain types incorrectly declared as independently realized Things

criteria.title: Theory supports the Purpose
criteria.claim: Require T1–T5 to link activities, intended outcomes, measures and limitations to P1. Model validation rejects missing measures or engagement substituted for wanted contact; pilot outcome hooks record support, challenge or unknown separately from conformance

criteria.title: Communication topology holds
criteria.claim: Require two-endpoint pairs, one target per outgoing direct action, private incoming aggregation and disabled group scope. Model validation rejects recipient arrays or an enabled digest without an accepted publication contract; C.webapp.outgoing.single supplies implementation evidence

criteria.title: Autonomy is preserved
criteria.claim: Require owner-only goals and notes, explicit consent, revocation and notification bounds across enabled scope. A coverage hook must resolve these obligations to C.webapp.private.owner, C.webapp.connection.consent, C.webapp.revocation.current and C.webapp.prompts.bounded
